title: v2 stores (seeded): a log read never fails on a line still being written
head: d44018462733ff9d6c6f71fd401237822d8dfa2d
brief: _read_lines reads an append-only JSONL log without the writer's lock. Only the last line, and only when the file does not end in a newline, can be a write in progress; if it does not parse (or ends mid-character) it is left out. Everything else stays an error: an interior or newline-terminated bad line is corruption and raises StoreError with a path:N: message. Records end at the newline only (U+2028 and friends are data). Tests: torn_read and separator_characters in tests/v2/stores_check.py.
focus: only the final unterminated line is forgiven

seeded.description: the in-progress-write exemption in _read_lines covers the last two lines instead of the last line
seeded.patch:
diff --git a/jarvis/v2/stores.py b/jarvis/v2/stores.py
index 2b49e31..04b7033 100644
--- a/jarvis/v2/stores.py
+++ b/jarvis/v2/stores.py
@@ -142,7 +142,7 @@ def _read_lines(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
         try:
             item = json.loads(line)
         except ValueError as exc:
-            if unfinished and number == len(lines):
+            if unfinished and number >= len(lines) - 1:
                 break                  # a write in progress, not corruption
             raise StoreError(f"{path}:{number}: {exc}") from exc
         if not isinstance(item, dict):

ground_truth.mechanism: the torn-write exemption is off by one: a bad line that is second to last is now treated as a write in progress, so an unterminated file whose second-to-last record is corrupt is silently cut short there, dropping the corrupt record and the valid final record instead of raising
ground_truth.evidence: file 'good\nBAD\n{"x":1}' (no trailing newline): read returns only the first row where the contract is StoreError at line 2
